function_extent.frame: no EBP frame; three callee-saved registers pushed and popped, EBX/ESI/EDI

observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: Modelled from the machine, not from the SDK label. EAX is written exactly twice in the whole body: MOV EAX,0x1 at 0x00f968ef on the all-compares-matched path and XOR EAX,EAX at 0x00f968fa on every other path, so the full 32-bit register is 0 or 1 and the function is a predicate. Ghidra's persisted signature claims 'Raster *' for this VA; that label is contradicted by the two writes above and no pointer value is ever formed, so bool is what the source span declares. A 0/1-valued pointer return cannot be excluded from this body alone.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: EAX is 1 only when the +0x58 slot answered the address of receiver+0x04 for selector id 0x8 AND for selector id 0x7; EAX is 0 on the first mismatch and on the second mismatch
observed_original_abi.saved_registers: EBX, ESI, EDI - pushed at 0x00f968b0, 0x00f968b1 and 0x00f968b4, popped at 0x00f968ed/0x00f968ee and 0x00f968f8/0x00f968f9, with EBX popped last at 0x00f968f4 and 0x00f968fc
observed_original_abi.frame: no EBP frame and no local storage; every value the body needs is either in a register or re-read from the argument
observed_original_abi.stack_argument_observation: The single ordinary argument is read as MOV EBX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10] at 0x00f968c0, i.e. at entry_ESP + 4 because three registers were already pushed; it is then used as a POINTER (MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBX] at 0x00f968c4 and 0x00f968de, loading the callee's vtable) and also as the callee's receiver (MOV ECX,EBX at 0x00f968cb and 0x00f968e5). Ghidra's parameter name 'int quadIndex' is therefore wrong: the slot is dereferenced, never used as a value.
observed_original_abi.termination: returns to the caller from either RET 0x4; there is no tail call, no exception path and no loop

observed_mechanics: 0x00f968b2 MOV ESI,ECX - the receiver is taken from ECX and kept in ESI for the whole body; ESI is callee-saved so the value survives both indirect calls.
0x00f968b5..0x00f968be - a null receiver does not abort: the anchor is materialised as 0 (XOR EDI,EDI), so the two compares then test the provider's answers against NULL.
0x00f968c0 MOV EBX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x10] - the sole ordinary stack argument, read after the three prologue pushes, i.e. at entry_ESP+4, and kept in the callee-saved EBX across both calls.
0x00f968c4 and 0x00f968de MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBX] - the argument is an object pointer: its first dword is the vtable, and the argument itself (not the receiver) is the callee's this (MOV ECX,EBX).
0x00f968c6 and 0x00f968e0 MOV EDX,dword ptr [EAX + 0x58] - the same slot, byte offset 0x58 (index 22), is dispatched twice; the second dispatch re-reads the word from memory instead of reusing EDX.
0x00f968c9 PUSH 0x8 then 0x00f968e3 PUSH 0x7 - two selector ids, 0x8 first, each the callee's only stack argument.
0x00f968cf CMP EAX,EDI and 0x00f968e9 CMP EAX,ESI - both compares test the callee's returned POINTER against the ADDRESS of the receiver's field at +0x04, the same address in both cases.
0x00f968d1 and 0x00f968eb - both mismatches branch to the same epilogue at 0x00f968f8, so the second query is short-circuited by the first and EAX is 1 only when both answers match.
0x00f968ef MOV EAX,0x1 / 0x00f968fa XOR EAX,EAX - the entire 32-bit EAX is written with 1 or 0; the body is a predicate, not a pointer producer.
0x00f968f5 and 0x00f968fd RET 0x4 - the callee pops the single stack word, so the argument is __thiscall callee-cleanup.
No global is read or written, no stack slot below the entry frame is touched, and the body contains no loop, no arithmetic on data and no call other than the two slot dispatches.

semantic_findings.kind: virtual predicate over a caller-supplied provider
semantic_findings.statement: The function asks the provider for two different things (ids 0x8 and 0x7 through vtable slot +0x58) and succeeds only when BOTH answers are the address of its own field at +0x04.
semantic_findings.short_circuit: The id 0x7 query is issued only if the id 0x8 query already answered the anchor (0x00f968d1 jumps past it).
semantic_findings.null_receiver_behaviour: With a NULL receiver the anchor is 0 in both compares, so the function returns 1 exactly when the provider answers NULL to both ids. This is what the compiler emits for a guard on a member address; whether the source contained an explicit null test is not decidable.
semantic_findings.no_side_effects: The body mutates no state of its own and no global; the only writes are to EAX and to the stack in the prologue.
semantic_findings.callee_is_observed_indirectly: The provider's vtable word is read twice rather than cached, so a provider that replaces its own vtable between the two queries is honoured by the second compare.

decompilation_defects_corrected: The persisted export .spore-analysis/ghidra-exports/decompiled_sdk/Terrain__cTerrainSphere__GetSimDataRTT.c types the dispatch as '(*this->_vftable0->RemoveModelModification)(&DAT_00000008, ...)'. The machine loads the vtable from the STACK ARGUMENT (MOV EAX,dword ptr [EBX]), not from the receiver, and the pushed word is an immediate 0x8/0x7, not the address of a DAT_ symbol. Corrected to provider->vtable->select_58(provider, 0x8).

The same export invents unaff_EDI, unaff_EBX, unaff_SI, unaff_retaddr and in_ECX as separate values. The machine reloads the provider from [ESP+0x10] into EBX and reuses ESI, so those registers are not independent inputs; the argument is read once and kept.

The export's bVar1/extraout_var pair (CONCAT31(extraout_var, bVar1)) is a decompiler artefact of an indirect __thiscall whose EAX is compared as a pointer; the callee's return is a pointer, not a byte flag.

The export returns 'Raster *' and the Ghidra signature is 'Raster *(cTerrainSphere *, int quadIndex)'. The body writes EAX with 1 or 0 only, and it dereferences the second argument twice, so neither the return type nor the int parameter survives contact with the bytes. Modelled as bool returning, with a pointer-shaped argument.
decompilation_agreements_kept_as_evidenc: The receiver is the ECX argument and the body is short with two calls: the export and the byte image agree on that much.
The export's control shape - a first comparison that, when it fails, skips the second, and a success value of exactly 1 - matches 0x00f968d1/0x00f968ef.

placement_in_a_vtable.corroboration: ghidra_get_xrefs_to(0x00f968b0) returns exactly one reference and it is DATA from 0x01490c7c; 0x01490c7c - 0x01490be8 = 0x94. No call edge points at the entry, which is what a table entry looks like.
placement_in_a_vtable.known_sibling_entries: 0x00f96870 appears twice in this table (0x01490c1c, slot 13, and 0x01490c80, slot 38) and 0x00f96900 is slot 39. 0x00f96870 is the entry whose body this package used to date the receiver's sibling pointers at +0x30, +0x74, +0xb8 and +0xfc.

validation.focused_test_result: PASS - 5 scenarios, 11 assertions, exit 0, no compiler diagnostics under -Wall -Wextra -Werror
validation.codegen_cross_check: At -O2 -m32 GCC 16 emits lea ebx,4[ecx] / cmove ebx,ecx, mov eax,[esi] / mov ecx,esi / push 8 / call [eax+0x58], cmp ebx,eax / je, then the same sequence with push 7 and sete al, and ret 4. Slot offset 0x58, both selector ids, the anchor address, the short circuit, the callee-cleaned single argument and the 0/1-in-EAX outcome all reproduce; GCC folds the second anchor computation into EBX and writes the success value with SETE AL, so only AL is defined on the true path whereas the original MOV EAX,0x1 defines all 32 bits.

confidence_note: The mechanics are CONFIRMED and byte-exact: 39 instructions and 80 bytes from two agreeing live reads, one ECX receiver, one callee-cleaned pointer argument, two indirect calls at the single slot +0x58 with the immediates 0x8 and 0x7, two pointer compares against receiver+0x04, two branches to a shared zero-return epilogue, and EAX written with exactly 0 or 1. The model compiles warning-free on x86-32 and its codegen reproduces the observed shape. Confidence is held below the 0.9 band by four unresolved items, none of which affect the mechanics: the return type disagrees with the Ghidra/SDK label, the argument's declared type is unknown, the +0x58 slot's owning class is unidentified, and the reason the same anchor is compared against two selector ids cannot be decided from this body.
unresolved_questions: Return type: the machine writes EAX with 1 (0x00f968ef) or 0 (0x00f968fa) and nothing else, so the source span declares bool; Ghidra's persisted signature and the SDK-derived label say 'Raster *'. A 0/1-valued pointer return cannot be excluded from this body alone. If the integrator prefers the pointer reading, the span's return type and this sidecar's observed_original_abi.return_type must change together.

The declared type of the second parameter is unknown. Ghidra calls it 'int quadIndex', but the body dereferences it twice as an object pointer and passes it as the callee's this, so the label is wrong; the owning class of vtable slot +0x58 is unidentified (the dispatch is register-indirect, so no xref names the implementation).

Why the same address (receiver+0x04) is compared against two different selector ids cannot be decided from this body: it is equally consistent with source that queried the provider twice and with a compiler that duplicated an anchor load around an inlined call. The staged model reproduces the machine, not the intent.

The extents are not observable here. Only addresses of the anchored sub-object are taken, so neither its size nor the receiver's size follows from this target; the receiver's 0x100 modelled extent and the sibling pointers at +0x30/+0x74/+0xb8/+0xfc are borrowed from the sibling virtual 0x00f96870 in the same vtable, and the anchored sub-object's 4-byte blob is a modelling floor only.

The owner of vtable:0x01490be8 was not established: the Ghidra label is address-only, its two xrefs were not traced to a constructor, and whether cTerrainSphere has a second vtable (the briefing lists vtable:0x01490c7c, which is this function's own slot) is open.
No caller exists in the image, so the caller's expected argument, whether the id 0x8/0x7 answers are meant to alias one object, and whether the null-receiver path is reachable are all unobserved.

The briefing's single analogue (PKG-16-SPOREPEDIA-ONLINE, 0x00641770, matched on shared_vtable vtable:0x01490be8) is not usable prior art: 0x00641770 sits at slot index 2 of that table and is a Sporepedia asset-data predicate, so the match basis is a slot-index coincidence, not a shared class.
